aiReview.summary: This express@4.18.2 package contains the standard Express framework code and does not perform any install-time actions, network calls, or secret exfiltration in its entry or install files.
aiReview.reasoning: I inspected the entry point (index.js) and the main module (lib/express.js). index.js simply exports lib/express. lib/express.js constructs the Express application, exposes middleware and constructors, and references common dependencies (body-parser, serve-static) without executing external commands or performing I/O at import time. Searches for suspicious patterns (child_process, exec, process.env usage beyond NODE_ENV) found only a NODE_ENV read in lib/application.js and no spawn/exec/fetch/http request code. No preinstall/install/postinstall scripts were present in the package listing. The behavior matches the package description (web framework) and typical code structure for Express.

evidence.explanation: createApplication function builds app and calls app.init(), typical framework behavior; no network or shell calls.
Exposes middleware and references body-parser and serve-static, benign dependencies.
Only reads process.env.NODE_ENV, normal for config.

findingAssessments.explanation: Package listing shows no install-time (pre/post install) scripts or files that run at install.
index.js only exports lib/express; import has no side-effects beyond typical module initialization.
Searches for child_process, exec, and network calls found none; code uses standard Express constructs.
